claims: David Barrett is the singer, songwriter, and composer behind "One Shining Moment," the anthem for the NCAA March Madness tournament.
David Barrett wrote and recorded the original version of "One Shining Moment" in 1986.
David Barrett sang the original version of "One Shining Moment".
Luther Vandross performed a version of "One Shining Moment" used in the NCAA March Madness tournament.
Teddy Pendergrass performed a version of "One Shining Moment" used in the NCAA March Madness tournament.
David Barrett was inspired by watching Larry Bird on TV at a bar in East Lansing, Michigan, in 1986.
"One Shining Moment" has been the traditional song played at the end of the final game's highlight reel since the 1987 NCAA Championship.
Teddy Pendergrass recorded a version of "One Shining Moment" used in the 1994 NCAA March Madness tournament.
